process.heading: How an Edstellar leadership coaching program runs.
process.description: Six steps take each leader from nomination to a final summary they control, over six to eight months. Your CHRO sees progress at every step; the coaching itself stays between leader and coach.

steps.label: Nominate leaders
steps.title: Nominate leaders
steps.description: Your CHRO or program admin adds each leader on Meridian with their role, objective and focus areas. The leader agrees to take part.

steps.label: Match a leadership coach
steps.title: Match a leadership coach
steps.description: In a 30-minute video session, the leader reviews the certified coaches Meridian recommends and chooses one. The CHRO can join this session if the leader wants them there.

steps.label: Chemistry session
steps.title: Chemistry session
steps.description: A free 30-minute session to test the fit, confirm the objective, choose one of the six leadership tracks and agree the schedule.
steps.who: Leader and coach · live on video

steps.label: Coaching sessions
steps.title: Coaching sessions
steps.description: Ten to twelve hours of one-on-one coaching on Meridian. The leader sets the focus, the coach prepares, and an assignment carries the work forward.
steps.who: Leader and coach · live on video

steps.label: Mid-point check-in
steps.title: Mid-point check-in
steps.description: Halfway through, leader and coach review progress against the objective and adjust the plan for the hours ahead.
steps.who: Leader and coach · live on video

steps.label: Final review and summary
steps.title: Final review and summary
steps.description: The final session agrees what the leader will keep doing, and the leader chooses what the CHRO sees in the final summary.

items.question: What is leadership coaching?
items.answer: Leadership coaching is one-on-one professional coaching for directors, senior managers and high-potential leaders, focused on growing the skills, identity and confidence needed to lead people and teams well. Edstellar's leadership coaching pairs each leader with a certified coach for ten to twelve hours over six to eight months, run on Meridian.

items.question: Who is leadership coaching for?
items.answer: Leadership coaching is for newly promoted directors, high-potentials in your pipeline, senior managers taking on wider scope and experts transitioning into leading other managers.

items.question: How long does a leadership coaching engagement last?
items.answer: Ten to twelve hours of one-on-one coaching over six to eight months. The session length and schedule are agreed in the free chemistry session.

items.question: What certifications do Edstellar leadership coaches hold?
items.answer: Every Edstellar leadership coach is certified by the International Coaching Federation (ICF) at PCC or MCC level, the International Coaching Community (ICC) or the European Mentoring and Coaching Council (EMCC). Coaches are also vetted by Edstellar before Meridian can recommend them.

items.question: How does Edstellar match a leader with a coach?
items.answer: Meridian recommends certified coaches based on the leader's track, objective, language and time zone. In a 30-minute video session the leader reviews the recommendations and chooses one, then meets the coach in a free chemistry session before anyone commits.

items.question: What does our organization see during leadership coaching?
items.answer: Your CHRO sees sessions held, hours used, progress against the agreed objective and the parts of the final summary the leader chooses to share. Session content, notes and assignments stay between leader and coach.

items.question: What are the six leadership coaching tracks?
items.answer: Leadership Identity, Delegation & Trust, Difficult Conversations, Building the Team, Leading Change and Influence Without Authority. The leader chooses one with the coach in the chemistry session.

items.question: Is leadership coaching delivered virtually?
items.answer: Yes. Edstellar delivers leadership coaching virtually on Meridian, with every session on video and leaders seeing times in their own time zone. Language and time zone are part of how coaches are matched.
